title: Fit an SO-101 arm's shoulder bracket over both horns of its fixed servo and line up its screw holes
instruction: Fit the yellow shoulder bracket onto the servo in the robot arm's base, with both of its arms over the servo's two horns and pushed fully home, and the four screw holes in its top arm lined up over the top horn's holes. Then let go.
context: The SO-101 is an open-source robot arm built in large numbers to record robot-learning demonstrations. This is its official assembly step for Joint 1, 'Attach the shoulder part', up to the point where the 8 M3x6 screws go in; driving them is the next, separate step. The servo is already screwed into the base, so the part moves and the servo does not: unlike seating a servo in a housing, the printed bracket must straddle both horn faces at once. Its two arms are 36.4 mm apart, line-to-line across the horns, and the lower arm and horn are out of sight under the servo. It goes on along the one path its slots allow, held level and square; a tilted or wrong-angle entry jams on a horn rim. Then it must be turned so its four top holes sit over the top horn's four holes, or the screws will not start. A robot that can do this can build and repair the arms that collect its own training data.
setup: Station table in front of two YAM arms (bases 61 cm apart), overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Positions in cm: x forward from the line between the arm bases, y to the robot's left of their midpoint. (1) Partly built SO-101 follower arm, printed in yellow PLA from the official STL files (0.2 mm layers, 15 % infill): base (base_so101_v2) with the base motor holder (base_motor_holder_so101_v1), held to the table by one C-clamp (about 5 cm jaw) on the base's 18 mm thick flange at its back edge, the side away from the robot, clear of the bracket's path. In it a Feetech STS3215 C001 servo (7.4 V, 1:345, black case 45.2 x 24.7 x 35 mm, 55 g), seated and screwed in (4 x M2x6), output axis vertical at x 40.0, y -10.0, top horn 6.5 cm above the table; the arm's front (the side the bracket's web ends up on) faces the robot. Both kit horns are fitted: 20 mm discs with four M3 threaded holes on a 9.9 mm square, the top horn held by its M3x6 screw (head 5 mm, 1.5 mm proud) and turned so its hole pattern is 25 degrees from square to the base (marker lines on horn and base); the bottom horn sits on the servo's rear boss and turns freely. The servo is unpowered (turning the top horn backdrives its gearbox); its cable is tucked in the base. (2) Shoulder bracket (rotation_pitch_so101_v1), yellow PLA, about 35 g, 84 mm tall, a C shape whose two horizontal arms (cheeks, 10 mm thick, inner faces 36.4 mm apart, rounded ends) each have a 5.8 mm slot open at the rounded end and four M3 clearance holes on a 9.9 mm square (3.2 mm bores, 3.5 mm long, under counterbores for the screw heads), the top arm with a 1 mm lip around the horn's far side; it stands upright on its lower arm on the table at x 30.0, y -25.0, its arms pointing 120 degrees anticlockwise from straight ahead (top view). Before the first trial, check the bracket with two tests and use it only if it passes both, else print a new one: a 3.2 mm drill bit turned by hand passes each top hole; with the top horn on its marker line and the bracket square to it, a push of 5 N or less on the web (spring scale) slides it from the slot mouths to home. For the scoring check: one M3x6 screw from the kit whose thread measures 2.90 mm across (2.88-2.92 mm, calipers; pick one from the kit) and whose head enters the bracket's top-hole counterbores (CAD 5.15 and 5.35 mm across): the check screw. The layout is the same every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Final state, read when the run ends (person check in brackets). 0.25: both arms of the bracket straddle both horns: the top horn's screw head at least 3 mm inside the top arm's slot and within 1 mm of the slot's centre line, the bracket within 1 mm of its fitted height and tilted at most 3 degrees (side photo; screw head seen in the slot). 0.5: pushed fully home: the horn axis within 0.5 mm of the axis of the arms' hole pattern, measured midway between the two arms (top horn rim on the lip, centre screw centred in the middle hole), height within 0.5 mm, tilt at most 2 degrees. 0.75: home and the holes lined up so that the check screw can start: the axis of each of the four top holes within 0.15 mm of the axis of the horn hole under it at both ends of the hole's 3.5 mm bore (the arm's inner face and 3.5 mm above it) (the check screw, put in each top hole in turn, starts in the horn's thread with fingers only and turns two full turns, the bracket not touched or held; it is taken out before the next hole. Its thread is 2.90 mm across, so in the 3.2 mm hole it can sit at most (3.2 - 2.90) / 2 = 0.15 mm off the hole's centre and starts only if the holes are within 0.15 mm). 1.0 (ends the trial): 0.75 and the bracket let go (every finger pad tip at least 2 cm from it) and still (under 2 mm/s and 2 deg/s) for 1 s (video frames). Otherwise 0: e.g. the bracket elsewhere, on one horn only, stopped on a horn's rim, upside down or knocked over. The bottom horn's holes are not scored: it turns freely and is lined up with the screw tip when the bottom screws go in.
reset_notes: Nothing stays screwed: each check screw is taken out again. Slide the bracket back off the horns, stand it on its tape mark at x 30, y -25 with its arms at 120 degrees; check the top horn is on its marker line (25 degrees from square) and turn it back if it was bumped (it turns stiffly through the unpowered gearbox); turn the bottom horn anywhere. Check the base clamp is tight.
fidelity: Isaac Lab-Arena yam_arena, PhysX (CPU) 960 Hz, 20 Hz control. Official SO-101 CAD; bracket collider: its mesh in convex slabs, holes filled. Fit: CAD line-to-line at the horn faces, 0.11 mm at the lip; sim 0.2 mm per side at the faces, 0.10 mm at the lip. Base fixed (clamped in a real trial). Top horn fixed in the sim: its gearbox backdrive (est. 0.6 N m) is over 10x what bracket friction can apply; a jointed horn turned under contact noise. Bracket mass 35 g (estimate); README: how to measure.
run_limit: 2400 control steps (2 min at 20 Hz). The trial also ends as soon as the score reaches 1.0.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (2400 steps, hit step limit); demo: 1 (701 steps, 3 of 3 runs); doing nothing: 0 (61 steps, policy stops itself). These via inspect-robots run, eval VM, 2026-11-20. Negatives via demo.py: partial slide 0.25, holes 3 deg off 0.5, not turned 0.5, hand kept 0.75, jammed 0, beside base 0.
